content:
On the eve of a major iPhone launch event, Apple has just released the new iOS 26.6.2 software update for iPhone. Here's what the update includes.

iOS 26.6.2 fixes an issue that prevented software updates over cellular networks

Apple is expected to release iOS 27 in the near future, likely as early as next week.

However, ahead of this major release, Apple today rolled out the smaller iOS 26.6.2 update.

You can install iOS 26.6.2 on your iPhone by going to the "Software Update" section in "Settings".

Below is Apple's official release notes:

Given the bug fixes this update brings, it's a sensible move to release iOS 26.6.2 on the eve of the expected iOS 27 launch.

If iOS 26.6.1 left users unable to install iOS 27 over cellular, that would have been a big headache for Apple and its users next week.

However, by releasing this update ahead of time, the hope is that many iPhones will already have the necessary fix before attempting to install the much-anticipated iOS 27.

So there's nothing particularly noteworthy about this update itself, but its timing—just before iOS 27 and its many new features arrive—couldn't be better.

In addition to iOS 26.6.2, Apple also released iPadOS 26.6.2 for iPad at the same time, providing the exact same bug fixes.

Have you installed iOS 26.6.2 yet? Have you noticed any other changes? Let us know in the comments.
